# Statistics and comparison brackets

::: {.doc-lead}
Compute reporting rows with effect sizes and intervals, then attach the same results to a plot.
:::

## Two-group comparisons

Each two-group test takes two samples `(a, b)`, orients signs as `a − b`, and returns one
reporting row: a dict ready to save as a CSV in the plot's `_stats`
[dissection](/docs/dissections.html).

```python
import polars as pl
import fluxplot as fp

# sd_values and sleep_values are the two samples from your analysis.
row = fp.stats.welch_hedges(sd_values, sleep_values, names=("SD", "sleep"))
pl.DataFrame([row]).write_csv("plots/_dissections/app_gapdh/_stats/welch_ttest.csv")
```

The tests are two-sided unless you pass `alternative=`. A row's keys, in the order of
`fp.stats.REPORT_COLUMNS`, are:

- **Test and result**: `sig_test_used`, `test_statistic_value`, `p-value`, `p_corrected_holm`, `dof`.
- **Effect size**: `effect_size_method`, `effect_size_value`, `effect_size_95_CI`, and the
  interval as numbers in `effect_size_ci_low` and `effect_size_ci_high`.
- **Samples**: `n_a`, `n_b`, `n_total`, and `groups` (the names compared).
- **Also recorded**: `alternative`, `p_corrected_bh`, `dof_error`.

| Function | Design | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `welch_hedges` | independent samples, means | Welch's t-test |
| `mann_whitney_cliff` | independent samples, ranks | Mann–Whitney U (the `U` of `a`) |
| `paired_t_hedges` | paired samples, mean difference | paired t-test |
| `wilcoxon_rank_biserial` | paired samples, ranks | Wilcoxon signed-rank (`W+`, zeros dropped) |

Each reports this effect size with a 95% confidence interval:

| Function | Effect size and 95% CI |
|---|---|
| `welch_hedges` | Hedges' g with the non-pooled SD, `sqrt((var_a + var_b) / 2)`; Bonett (2008) CI |
| `mann_whitney_cliff` | Cliff's delta; Newcombe (2006) Method 5 score CI |
| `paired_t_hedges` | Hedges' g_z (SD of the differences); exact noncentral-t CI |
| `wilcoxon_rank_biserial` | Kerby's matched-pairs rank-biserial r; score CI |

The CIs target the population effect size, so they are never multiplied by Hedges' `J`. Both
rank-based CIs stay non-degenerate at complete separation (`delta` or `r` = ±1), which is common at
n = 6. Rank tests report `dof = None`. fluxplot's test suite (`tests/test_stats.py`) checks each
test against SciPy and against the equation that defines its interval.

## Multiple comparisons

A row on its own has `p_corrected_holm == p-value` (a family of one).
Holm's step-down correction needs every p-value in the family, so it is a separate pass over the
rows of the comparisons that belong together (e.g. every measure tested on the same animals in one
figure); extra keys such as a measure name ride along:

```python
# sd and sleep map each measure name to its samples.
rows = [dict(measure=m, **fp.stats.welch_hedges(sd[m], sleep[m])) for m in measures]
# Fill p_corrected_holm across the family; the row order is kept.
rows = fp.stats.holm(rows)
```

`fp.stats.holm_adjusted(p)` does the same for a bare array of p-values; `fp.stats.bh(rows)` /
`bh_adjusted(p)` fill `p_corrected_bh` with Benjamini–Hochberg (false-discovery-rate) values for a
screen of many measures. NaN p-values pass through both untouched.

## Three or more groups

The omnibus tests return one row, in which `groups` lists every group and F tests carry `dof`
and `dof_error`. The post-hoc tests return one row per pair. `pairwise` runs any two-group test
above over the pairs of a `{name: sample}` family and corrects across them.

| Function | Test | Effect size and 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| `anova_oneway` | one-way ANOVA | η² or ω² (`effect="eta2"` or `"omega2"`); Steiger's noncentral-F CI |
| `welch_anova` | Welch's ANOVA | ω²; noncentral-F CI on Welch's dof |
| `kruskal_epsilon` | Kruskal–Wallis | ε² = H / (N − 1); seeded bootstrap CI |
| `rm_anova` | repeated-measures ANOVA | partial η²; noncentral-F CI |
| `friedman_kendall` | Friedman | Kendall's W; seeded bootstrap CI |
| `tukey_hsd` | Tukey HSD | Hedges' g, pooled SD |
| `games_howell` | Games–Howell | Hedges' g, non-pooled SD; Bonett CI |
| `dunn` | Dunn's test | Cliff's delta; Newcombe CI |
| `pairwise` | any two-group test, per pair | the chosen test's |

Notes on the tests:

- `rm_anova` reports Greenhouse–Geisser-corrected degrees of freedom and p.
- `tukey_hsd` reports Tukey's family-wise p as it is, without a further correction.
- `games_howell` uses the studentized range on Welch's degrees of freedom.
- `dunn` is Dunn's rank-sum test after Kruskal–Wallis, corrected with `adjust="holm"` by default.
- `pairwise` corrects across the pairs with `adjust="holm"` (the default) or `"bh"`.

The group-based functions take the samples as positional arguments with optional `names=`, for
example `fp.stats.welch_anova(ctl, drug, sham, names=("ctl", "drug", "sham"))`. The
repeated-measures functions take a long table and its column names:
`fp.stats.rm_anova(table, subject, within, dv)`. Exact signatures are in the
[API reference](/docs/fluxplot-api.html#statistics). fluxplot's test suite
(`tests/test_stats_multi.py`) checks them against pingouin and scikit-posthocs reference values.

## Draw the comparisons

`fp.brackets(ax, rows, positions=…)` draws one significance bracket per
post-hoc row and stacks them automatically: shortest span first, each bracket one `step` above the
data it spans and above every bracket it overlaps in x (multiplicative steps on a log axis), so
nothing crosses. `positions` maps group name → x; a glowbar / fluxbox result provides it, and
`gb.brackets(rows)` is the one-liner:

```python
# ctl, drug and sham are the samples; df["group"] holds the same three names.
rows = fp.stats.pairwise(fp.stats.welch_hedges,
                         {"ctl": ctl, "drug": drug, "sham": sham})
gb = fp.glowbar(data=df, x="group", y="value", ax=ax)

# Stars (***, **, *, ns) from p_corrected_holm:
gb.brackets(rows)
# Or "p = 0.003" labels from the BH-corrected p-values, without the ns pairs:
gb.brackets(rows, label="p", ns=False, p_column="p_corrected_bh")
```

`label` is `"stars"`, `"p"`, `"both"` or a callable on the row. `thresholds`, `top`, `step` and
`tip` shape the stack, and extra keywords are passed to `fp.significance_bracket`. Each bracket's manifest
overlay carries `between: [a, b]`, `p` and a `stats` block — test, statistic, raw and corrected p,
correction, effect size and its CI, sizes — so the figure states exactly which test each star came
from.
